issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path; there is little troubleshooting for failed deployments, canary health failures, Vault JWT login errors, or placement failures beyond a brief mention.

The system job uses host network, host PID mode and a read-only root filesystem mount, but the skill explicitly warns that the client must enable these and tells the user to review the settings first.

scenarios.name: canary-deploy-with-plan-and-promote
scenarios.rationale: Both cover plan, run, promote, auto_revert and canary=1, but B uses the exact `-var image_tag=1.4.3` the rubric names while A uses `-var 'version=1.4.3'`, and B states the canary and auto_revert behaviour concisely; A is more thorough but diverges on the variable name.

scenarios.name: nightly-vault-backup-job
scenarios.rationale: Both use batch type, periodic with crons, time_zone UTC, prohibit_overlap and a template with env=true, but A uses the legacy `vault { policies }` stanza instead of the required `vault { role = ... }` (mentioning role only in a comment) and puts connection settings in an env block, while B uses `vault { role = ... }` exactly as required and keeps credentials out of env.

scenarios.name: per-node-exporter-system-job
scenarios.rationale: B uses the system job, static 9100, docker host network and pid mode, a read-only volume mount, a pinned tag, and an explicit warning that the Docker driver rejects pid_mode host and volume mounts without plugin docker config volumes enabled. A covers most of this but omits pid_mode = host from the spec, only mentions it in passing, and uses a mount block rather than the host volume the rubric describes, so it is weaker on the pid_mode warning.
